cells.tense: Right now you are at the shared table with the pen, and the ruling is yours to set down.
cells.act: build the change by persistent work
cells.ask: Pick the practice at your table that still earns its keep, name the smallest change that would strengthen it, and go do that much this week, steadily, unannounced.
cells.core:
You can decide at the shared table by what a practice has actually proven, and keep it going without turning the deciding into a fight. A ritual that has shown itself worth the hours stays strong under your hand; you do not need to defend it to anyone, and the table can feel that you have earned your say. The work keeps the thing alive and the thing keeps you in it.

That is where it stands today, practice carrying the group rather than the group carrying practice. Keep it there by building the one change you believe in through steady effort — the small repair, the one whose finish line you can already picture. The longer effort is what makes a thing worth handing over. What the line holds is not a rule; it is a practice somebody decided to keep.
cells.sheetLine: You can carry a shared practice forward by knowing what has earned its place.
cells.verb: Deciding with the precision of someone who has done the work
cells.place: Where meaning is carried between people and across time

cells.tense: You are bracing somewhere ahead of the calendar, where the shared thing must be settled before it has even been tried.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Name the practice you keep pushing on and decide, this week, whether it is finished; if it is, stop carrying it and give those hours to the one still alive. Nothing after.
cells.core:
Method is being pushed past what the shared thing can take. There is a way the group does something, and you are correcting it from a season the others have not walked into yet — the practice is being tightened before anyone has had a chance to see whether it holds. Nobody is refusing your standards; they cannot find you beside them, because you are standing where the thing already should have finished.

What is missing is not more rigor. It is the readiness to let a practice be complete and hand the floor to the ones still living. Practice without force is the other face of what you do — refinement that serves the group, not the worry that outruns it. Whatever you touch with that readiness will get your standard anyway, since you bring it everywhere.
cells.sheetLine: You are fixing the shared thing before it has had a chance to live.

cells.tense: You once had ways of carrying the shared thing, and you are still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Tell someone, aloud or on paper, what one thing between you took from them and what it gave — a favor owed, a wrong done, anything left unbalanced.
cells.core:
The shared practice used to be where you were most yourself, and you have stepped back. The reason is not carelessness: some imbalance between two people is sitting unfixed, and calling it fair again would mean being present where it happened. So you have stayed on the edge of the group, precise and quiet, and the shared thing has gone on without the one who understood it best. What is left undone is a judgment about fairness — not the work itself.

Do that and the appetite comes back with it. What you will have is the shared thing meeting you again: the practice you know how to keep, and the ones who are still keeping it, with you inside rather than behind the door. Fairness grows when it is exercised, not when it is studied.
cells.sheetLine: You can tell what's fair here, and you have stopped saying it.
cells.verb: Deciding with the precision of someone who has done the work
cells.place: Where meaning is carried between people and across time

cells.tense: You are already writing how the group keeps its meaning, while saying the plan belongs to everyone else.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Follow the next step you can already half-see in a shared practice — do it yourself, and keep doing it, without waiting for anyone to agree it was your idea.
cells.core:
You are already the one who works out how the shared thing should run — what gets taught, what gets kept, what shape the next version takes. Ask you directly and you say you just follow what the group has agreed, or that you are keeping to yourself. But the group's version is coming, quietly, from your working out. It is the making of a thing with the name left off, and it is doing work nobody can check.

Underneath it is plain: the sharing is there, and the fresh eye has not come out to say what it is doing. Say what you are making before it is settled and let one other person see the first step still forming. You will not lose the practice by dreaming it out loud; you will only stop pretending the dream arrived by itself.
